subject: Service reachability impact — APAC & EU traffic guidance and post-incident steps
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Jun 2029 09:12:30 -0700
Subject: Service reachability impact — APAC & EU traffic guidance and post-incident steps

Hi Sara / Orbit team,

Quick update from my side — our detection systems flagged increased 5xxs and connection timeouts for inference endpoints serving APAC and parts of EU starting ~08:40 UTC. Engineering has identified a load-balancer configuration flapping in the cloud provider’s regional front door affecting a subset of edge PoPs.

Immediate guidance (what you can do in the next 30–60 minutes):
- Switch requests to our US ingress: set X-Redwood-Region: us or hit the explicit endpoint us-west-1.api.redwood.com. This routes to US pools where capacity is healthy.
- Reduce max_tokens to 512 if you send long-context batches — this lowers tail latency while we stabilize.
- If you use connection pooling, reduce keepalive timeout to 15s to force periodic reconnection while routing heals.

I’ve attached a short playbook with exact curl examples (apac-eu-reroute-playbook-v1.pdf) and a one-click header snippet (reroute-api-headers.txt). We expect mitigations to be in place within 2–3 hours; I’ll share a follow-up timeline and a scheduled postmortem invite shortly.

We’ll include SLA credit options if this meets the incident threshold — I’ll confirm with billing once we have the final window.

Apologies for the disruption — we realize this impacts your production workflows and are prioritizing it.

Next steps:
1) Try the US endpoint and reply with a quick confirmation (latency / error rate).
2) Accept the postmortem invite I’ll send in an hour for a 30-minute readout.

— Chloe
Chloe Martin

Chloe / team — quick engineering note for Orbit:

Root cause summary (preliminary): the regional front-door experienced a control-plane race during a routing update; BGP/edge reconfiguration caused inconsistent hashes so some sessions were dropped intermittently. The model-serving clusters themselves remained healthy.

Short-term mitigations we pushed (08:55–09:45 UTC):
- Pinning: we forced traffic for affected regions onto the stable egress path (us-west-1) and disabled the problematic front-door route.
- Fallback: enabled a synchronous fallback that routes requests with header X-Redwood-Fallback: true to US pools when 502/504 observed.

Concrete steps for Orbit to minimize impact now:
1) Add header X-Redwood-Fallback: true to your call wrapper (see reroute-api-headers.txt).
2) Use the explicit host us-west-1.api.redwood.com (TLS remains the same, cert SANs include *.api.redwood.com — no need to update allowlists unless you restrict by egress IP; if you do, use the list in the attached playbook).

We are collecting request traces and will produce an evidence bundle for the requested window. ETA for full root-cause write-up: 48–72 hours.

On logs: we’ll hand over a sanitized trace archive (no customer payloads) and a signed timeline for compliance.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
